chapter: Fats Domino and rock and roll years
title: Recording with Fats Domino
summary: He worked and recorded with Fats Domino, playing on about half his records, and missed a Roy Brown session before Fats started.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Have you made many records with any of the singers, or do you sing yourself, by the way?
Well, I work with Fats Domino.
Did you ever record any, make, any of his records?
You're on some of his records, then?
I'm caught, in fact, uh, almost one half of the records he made.
Oh, really? I didn't even know. You see, they've...
Most everything he cut in town, I don't remember.
Yeah, most of those, they don't put the names of the band on, you know. Some records do, but his don't, I don't believe, usually.
And, uh, when I first started recording, I started recording with, uh, Rob Brown. Uh-huh. I was supposed to make the, uh, Round About Midnight, you know, Round About Midnight?
The Rock of Midnight with him. Uh-huh. And something happened, I didn't get on that, that session. And right after that, Fats Domino came to the scene, and, uh, and caught it.
Just about when did Fats Domino make those first records that made the big hits? How long ago, can you remember?
Well, uh, the Fat Man was the one that's supposed to have gotten started.
You remember about what year? I think that was around, 51.
About 1951, that long. That long ago, I couldn't remember.
